question: Long before modern labs, how did early humans figure out which foods were safe to eat?
explanation: Spot on! Before science labs, our ancestors had to rely on simple observation and trying things out to see what was safe to put in their bodies. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h1)

question: Why do we as nursing students need to look back at the history of nutrition?

options.A: To learn how to farm and produce raw food crops
options.B: To replace modern laboratory tests with ancient beliefs
options.C: To memorize the exact dates every vitamin was discovered
options.D: To understand how current dietary guidelines were developed

explanation: You got it! Knowing our history helps us see how past observations grew into the solid clinical recommendations we use to help patients today. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h1)

question: Which ancient group regularly practiced fasting and purging because they believed bad food caused all illnesses?
explanation: That's right! Ancient Egyptian records show they strongly linked diseases to diet, leading them to use routine purges to clear out sickness. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h2)

question: What did Hippocrates mean when he famously said, 'Let food be thy medicine'?

options.A: Food has no actual impact on human health
options.B: Patients should take drugs instead of eating meals
options.C: Only doctors are allowed to prepare daily meals
options.D: Diet plays a direct role in preventing and treating illness

explanation: Spot on! Hippocrates understood early on that what we eat directly shapes our health and healing journey. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h2)

question: Who is known as the father of nutrition for his early work on how our bodies use oxygen to burn food for energy?
explanation: Correct! Lavoisier used clever chemical experiments to show how respiration and metabolism tie directly into how we process food. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h3)

question: What famous milestone did James Lind achieve when he tested citrus fruits on sailors?

options.A: The chemical isolation of pure vitamin C in a laboratory
options.B: The creation of the first national food pyramid
options.C: An early controlled clinical trial using citrus fruits for scurvy
options.D: The discovery of complex carbohydrates in grains

explanation: You nailed it! Lind compared different treatments and proved that oranges and lemons could cure sailors suffering from scurvy. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h3)

question: What name did Casimir Funk originally give to essential food factors that he believed were life-giving amines?
explanation: That's correct! He combined 'vital' and 'amines' to coin the term 'vitamines' for these crucial health-boosting substances. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h4)

question: Why was the discovery of vitamins a massive turning point in healthcare?

options.A: It meant that eating enough total calories prevented all known illnesses
options.B: It eliminated the need for protein in the human diet
options.C: It proved diseases could happen simply from lacking small amounts of specific micronutrients
options.D: It showed that only wealthy people could ever suffer from nutritional disorders

explanation: Spot on! It opened our eyes to the fact that missing tiny trace elements, rather than just starving overall, could cause terrible diseases like scurvy. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h4)

question: When were the very first official Recommended Dietary Allowances introduced?

options.A: During the chemical revolution of Lavoisier
options.B: During the discovery of vitamin C

explanation: Correct! Governments needed a way to ensure soldiers and citizens stayed healthy despite wartime food rationing, so they set these standard allowances. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h5)

question: How do modern nutritional guidelines differ from the ones created in the early 20th century?

options.A: They now focus on preventing chronic diseases in addition to stopping deficiencies
options.B: They have completely removed any guidelines regarding vitamins and minerals
options.C: They only focus on calculating the exact amount of daily calories needed
options.D: They are designed exclusively for treating severe hospital patients

explanation: You got it! While older guidelines just wanted to stop diseases like rickets, today we also look at long-term wellness, like preventing heart disease and obesity. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h5)

question: Which of these crops make up the traditional, local staple foods in Nigerian diets?
explanation: Spot on! Traditional Nigerian diets rely heavily on locally grown grains, tubers, and legumes that thrive right here in our climate. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h6)

question: As a Nigerian nurse, what is a key part of your role when it comes to community nutrition?

options.A: Formulating industrial food additives in factories
options.B: Replacing all traditional farming with foreign grains
options.C: Educating communities and managing cases of malnutrition
options.D: Exporting local cash crops to international markets

explanation: That's right! Nurses are frontline educators. We spot nutritional gaps in our clinics and teach mothers the best ways to feed their families. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h6)

question: What is the core focus of the modern field called nutrigenomics?

options.A: How to grow crops without using water
options.B: How to eliminate all fats from human diets
options.C: How to manufacture artificial synthetic vitamins
options.D: How food and nutrients interact with human genes

explanation: Brilliant! Nutrigenomics looks at the cool science of how your unique genetic makeup changes the way your body responds to the food you eat. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h7)

question: What major nutrition paradox do we see in many societies today?

options.A: Vitamin deficiencies have completely disappeared from all populations
options.B: Undernutrition coexists with high rates of obesity and chronic illness
options.C: Everyone in the world now has access to too much food
options.D: People no longer eat carbohydrates or fats anywhere

explanation: You nailed it! It's striking how many communities battle hunger and undernutrition on one side, while fighting lifestyle-related obesity and chronic illness on the other. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h7)
